title: Broadband bill higher because promotional discount ended
body:
# Broadband bill higher because promotional discount ended

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My broadband bill is higher than usual this month.
- The monthly price went up without warning.
- I am being charged more than the price I signed up for.

## Likely cause
The introductory discount period ended, so the bill went up to the standard price.

## Resolution steps
1. Compare the current bill with the previous bill line by line.
2. Check whether a promotional discount ended and on what date.
3. Explain the change and show where the end date was stated in the contract.
4. Check which retention offers the customer is eligible for and apply one if accepted.
5. Confirm the new monthly price in writing.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the retention team if the customer asks to cancel.

title: Charged an installation fee that was promised free
body:
# Charged an installation fee that was promised free

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I was charged an installation fee that was supposed to be free.
- My first bill has a setup charge I was told would be waived.
- There is an activation fee on my bill but the offer said free installation.

## Likely cause
The free-installation offer code was not applied to the order, so the standard fee was billed.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the order for the offer code and the terms the customer signed up to.
2. If free installation was part of the offer, credit the installation fee.
3. Add the missing offer code to the account so later bills are correct.
4. Tell the customer the credit will show on the next bill.
5. Report the missed offer to the sales quality team.

## When to escalate
Escalate to billing if the offer cannot be confirmed from the order or the call recording.

title: Payment made but service suspended because payment was not matched
body:
# Payment made but service suspended because payment was not matched

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I paid my bill but my internet has been cut off.
- My service was suspended even though I already paid.
- The payment went out of my bank but the account still shows unpaid.

## Likely cause
The payment was made with a wrong reference or is still in clearing, so the account shows unpaid and service was suspended.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask for the payment date, amount, method and reference number.
2. Search the unallocated payments for a payment that matches.
3. Allocate the payment to the correct account.
4. Lift the suspension and restore service immediately.
5. Remove any late payment fee and confirm the balance with the customer.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the payments team if the payment cannot be found within 24 hours of proof being supplied.

title: Automatic payment failed because the card expired
body:
# Automatic payment failed because the card expired

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My automatic payment failed this month.
- The direct debit did not go through.
- I got a message saying my payment was declined.

## Likely cause
The saved card expired or the bank declined it, so the automatic payment did not go through.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the reason for the payment failure on the account.
2. If the card has expired, ask the customer to update the card details in the app.
3. Take a one-off payment for the outstanding amount.
4. Confirm that automatic payment is active with the new card.
5. Waive the late payment fee if this is the first failure.

## When to escalate
No escalation needed. Refer the customer to their bank if the bank keeps declining a valid card.

title: Still billed after cancelling the service
body:
# Still billed after cancelling the service

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I cancelled my broadband but I am still being billed.
- You are still charging me after I closed my account.
- I got a bill for a service I cancelled last month.

## Likely cause
The cancellation request was not completed, so the account stayed active and bills continued.

## Resolution steps
1. Find the cancellation request and check its date and status.
2. If the request was made but not completed, close the account from the original request date.
3. Refund all charges made after the cancellation date.
4. Confirm that the equipment was returned and remove any equipment fee.
5. Send written confirmation of the closure and the final balance.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the complaints team if there is no record of the cancellation and the customer has proof.

title: Speed upgrade purchased but speed unchanged
body:
# Speed upgrade purchased but speed unchanged

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I upgraded to a faster fibre plan but my speed is the same.
- I am paying for the 900 Mbps plan and still get 100.
- The speed boost I bought has not been applied.

## Likely cause
The new speed profile was not pushed to the ONT, or the customer's router cannot go faster than the old speed.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that the plan change order is complete and what speed profile is on the ONT.
2. Re-push the new speed profile to the ONT.
3. Ask the customer to power cycle the ONT and the router.
4. Check that the router and the ethernet cable support gigabit speeds.
5. Ask for a wired speed test and confirm the new speed.

## When to escalate
Escalate to provisioning if the profile push fails twice.

title: Set-top box shows error E-102 and no signal
body:
# Set-top box shows error E-102 and no signal

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My TV box shows error E-102.
- The set-top box says no signal on all channels.
- Error E-102 on screen and no channels are working.

## Likely cause
The set-top box lost its authorisation or its link to the TV service, which shows as error E-102.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that the TV subscription on the account is active and paid.
2. Send an authorisation refresh signal to the set-top box.
3. Ask the customer to power cycle the set-top box and wait five minutes.
4. Check that the box is connected to the router and has a network connection.
5. If the error stays, send a replacement set-top box.

## When to escalate
Escalate to TV platform support if several customers report E-102 at the same time.

title: TV picture freezing and pixelating
body:
# TV picture freezing and pixelating

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- The TV picture keeps freezing.
- Channels are pixelating and the picture breaks up.
- The TV stutters and the sound cuts out.

## Likely cause
The set-top box is on weak Wi-Fi or the broadband is busy, so the TV stream breaks up.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the set-top box connection type and its signal strength.
2. Ask the customer to connect the box to the router with an ethernet cable.
3. If only Wi-Fi is possible, move the box closer to the router or add a mesh unit.
4. Run a broadband speed test to check there is enough bandwidth for TV.
5. Update the set-top box software.

## When to escalate
Raise a broadband speed fault if the line speed is below the TV minimum requirement.

title: Subscribed channel pack missing
body:
# Subscribed channel pack missing

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I subscribed to the sports pack but the channels are not showing.
- The movie channels I paid for are missing.
- My new channel pack is not available on the TV.

## Likely cause
The channel pack was added to the account but the entitlement was not sent to the set-top box.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that the channel pack is active on the account.
2. Send an entitlement refresh to the set-top box.
3. Ask the customer to restart the box and wait five minutes.
4. Check that the channel is part of the pack the customer bought.
5. Credit the days the pack was paid for but not available.

## When to escalate
Escalate to TV platform support if the entitlement refresh fails twice.

title: Crackling noise on landline calls
body:
# Crackling noise on landline calls

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- There is a crackling noise on my landline.
- My home phone line is very noisy.
- I can hear static on every landline call.

## Likely cause
A corroded joint, a faulty handset or a bad socket adds noise to the copper line.

## Resolution steps
1. Run a line test to check for noise or a low insulation fault.
2. Ask the customer to test with a corded phone in the master socket test port.
3. If the noise goes away, the fault is in the customer's handset or extension wiring.
4. If the noise stays, raise a line fault and book an engineer.
5. Tell the customer that broadband speed may also improve after the repair.

## When to escalate
Book an engineer if the line test shows a fault or the noise is present on the test port.

title: No dial tone on landline
body:
# No dial tone on landline

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My landline has no dial tone.
- The home phone is completely dead.
- I cannot make or receive calls on my landline.

## Likely cause
A line fault or a disconnected cable means the landline has no dial tone.

## Resolution steps
1. Check for a known fault or planned work in the area.
2. Run a line test to look for a disconnection or short circuit.
3. Ask the customer to test with a corded phone in the master socket test port.
4. If there is still no dial tone, raise a line fault and book an engineer.
5. Set up call divert to the customer's mobile until the line is fixed.

## When to escalate
Escalate as a priority fault if the customer is vulnerable or relies on the landline for an alarm.

title: Cannot log in to the app because the account is locked
body:
# Cannot log in to the app because the account is locked

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I cannot log in to the app.
- The app says my account is locked.
- My password is not being accepted in the app.

## Likely cause
Several failed login attempts locked the account, or the registered email is out of date.

## Resolution steps
1. Verify the customer's identity using the security questions.
2. Check whether the account is locked and unlock it.
3. Check that the registered email and mobile number are up to date.
4. Send a password reset link and stay with the customer while they log in.
5. Ask the customer to update the app to the latest version.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the digital support team if login fails after the unlock and password reset.

title: Evening broadband drops caused by peak-hour congestion
body:
# Evening broadband drops caused by peak-hour congestion

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My broadband drops every evening around 8pm.
- The internet cuts out most nights between 7 and 10.
- Every night at peak time my connection disconnects for a few minutes.

## Likely cause
The local exchange is congested between about 7pm and 10pm, so the line loses sync or slows to a crawl at peak time.

## Resolution steps
1. Run a remote line test and compare sync speed and error counts between daytime and 7pm to 10pm.
2. Check the exchange utilisation report for the customer's cabinet to confirm peak-hour congestion.
3. Change the router Wi-Fi channel to a less crowded one to rule out local interference.
4. Move the customer to a less loaded port or apply the congestion-relief profile.
5. If the cabinet is over capacity, raise a capacity ticket with the network team and give the customer the expected upgrade date.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the network capacity team if utilisation is above 90 percent for three evenings in a row.

title: Random broadband disconnects caused by faulty line filter or internal wiring
body:
# Random broadband disconnects caused by faulty line filter or internal wiring

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My broadband disconnects at random times during the day.
- The internet drops whenever the house phone rings.
- Connection keeps cutting out for a minute and then comes back, no pattern to it.

## Likely cause
A faulty microfilter, a loose cable or old extension wiring adds noise to the line, so the router loses sync at random times, often when the landline rings.

## Resolution steps
1. Run a line test and check for a high error count or frequent re-syncs.
2. Ask the customer to replace the microfilter on every socket that has a phone plugged in.
3. Ask the customer to plug the router into the master socket test port to bypass internal wiring.
4. If the line is stable on the test port, advise removing or replacing the extension wiring.
5. If re-syncs continue on the test port, book an engineer visit for a line fault.

## When to escalate
Book an engineer if more than five re-syncs per day continue on the master socket test port.

title: Total broadband outage with DSL light off due to line fault
body:
# Total broadband outage with DSL light off due to line fault

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My broadband is completely down and the DSL light is off.
- No internet at all since this morning, the router shows a red light.
- The internet has stopped working entirely.

## Likely cause
A physical fault on the copper line or at the cabinet means the router cannot sync at all.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the outage map for a known fault in the customer's area.
2. Run a remote line test to look for an open circuit or a loss of sync.
3. Ask the customer to connect the router to the master socket test port with a new cable.
4. If there is still no sync, raise a line fault and book the earliest engineer slot.
5. Offer a temporary mobile data add-on while the fault is open.

## When to escalate
Escalate as a priority fault if the customer is vulnerable or the outage exceeds 48 hours.

title: Fibre outage with red LOS light on the ONT
body:
# Fibre outage with red LOS light on the ONT

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My fibre is down and there is a red LOS light on the white box.
- No internet, the fibre box is showing a red light.
- Fibre connection stopped working and the LOS light is blinking red.

## Likely cause
The optical signal is lost because of a fibre cut, a bent or unplugged fibre patch lead, or an area outage.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the outage map for a fibre cut or planned work in the area.
2. Ask the customer to check that the fibre patch lead is firmly clicked in and not sharply bent.
3. Power cycle the ONT first and then the router, waiting two minutes between them.
4. Run a remote optical power test on the ONT.
5. If the LOS light stays red, raise a fibre fault and book an engineer.

## When to escalate
Escalate to field operations if several customers on the same splitter report a red LOS light.

title: Broadband speed far below plan all day due to line profile or old router
body:
# Broadband speed far below plan all day due to line profile or old router

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My broadband is very slow all day, far below what I pay for.
- I am paying for 80 Mbps but only getting 10.
- Internet speed has been terrible for weeks at every time of day.

## Likely cause
The line is stuck on a low-speed profile after earlier instability, or an old router cannot deliver the plan speed.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask for a wired speed test result and compare it with the line sync speed.
2. Check whether the line is on a banded or capped profile after past instability.
3. Reset the line profile so the speed can retrain over the next 48 hours.
4. Check the router model and replace it if it does not support the plan speed.
5. If sync speed is below the guaranteed minimum, raise a speed fault.

## When to escalate
Raise a speed fault if the wired speed stays below the guaranteed minimum after the profile reset.

title: Fibre slow on Wi-Fi only because devices use the 2.4 GHz band
body:
# Fibre slow on Wi-Fi only because devices use the 2.4 GHz band

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My fibre is fast on the cable but slow on Wi-Fi.
- Wi-Fi speed is much lower than my fibre plan speed.
- On my phone I only get 30 Mbps even though I have 500 Mbps fibre.

## Likely cause
The connection is fast on a cable, but devices are connecting on the crowded 2.4 GHz band or are too old for high Wi-Fi speeds.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm that the wired speed test matches the plan, so the fibre line itself is healthy.
2. Ask which Wi-Fi band the device is on and move it to the 5 GHz network.
3. Split the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz networks into separate names so devices stay on 5 GHz.
4. Change the 5 GHz channel width to 80 MHz and pick a clear channel.
5. Explain that older devices cannot reach full plan speed over Wi-Fi.

## When to escalate
No escalation needed unless the wired speed is also below the plan speed.

title: Weak Wi-Fi signal in rooms far from the router
body:
# Weak Wi-Fi signal in rooms far from the router

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- Wi-Fi signal is very weak upstairs.
- I get no Wi-Fi in the bedroom at the back of the house.
- The wireless signal does not reach the far rooms.

## Likely cause
Thick walls and distance weaken the signal, and the router is badly placed for the size of the home.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask where the router is placed and move it to a central, open, raised position.
2. Keep the router away from microwaves, cordless phones and thick walls.
3. Use the 2.4 GHz band for far rooms because it travels further.
4. Offer the mesh Wi-Fi add-on or a wired access point for large homes.
5. Confirm coverage with the customer using the app signal checker.

## When to escalate
No escalation needed. Offer a paid home Wi-Fi survey if mesh units do not help.

title: Router keeps rebooting by itself due to faulty hardware or power supply
body:
# Router keeps rebooting by itself due to faulty hardware or power supply

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My router keeps restarting by itself.
- The router reboots every few hours on its own.
- The router is very hot and switches itself off and on.

## Likely cause
A failing power adapter or overheating makes the router restart on its own.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the router uptime and reboot log remotely.
2. Ask the customer to use a different wall socket without an extension lead.
3. Make sure the router is in an open place and its vents are not covered.
4. Update the router firmware to the latest version.
5. If reboots continue, send a replacement router and power adapter.

## When to escalate
Send a replacement router if there are more than three unplanned reboots in 24 hours after the firmware update.

title: New fibre installed but service not activated
body:
# New fibre installed but service not activated

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- The engineer installed my fibre but it is still not working.
- My new fibre connection has not been activated yet.
- Fibre was installed three days ago and there is still no internet.

## Likely cause
The engineer completed the installation but the activation order is stuck in provisioning.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the order status and find the provisioning step that is stuck.
2. Confirm that the ONT serial number on the order matches the installed device.
3. Re-push the activation request from the provisioning system.
4. Ask the customer to power cycle the ONT and router once activation shows complete.
5. Apply a credit for the days without service after the install date.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the provisioning team if activation fails twice.

title: Broadband not transferred after house move
body:
# Broadband not transferred after house move

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I moved house and my broadband has not been moved to the new address.
- My internet was supposed to be transferred on moving day but it is not working.
- We have moved home and there is no broadband at the new place.

## Likely cause
The home move order was not completed, so the service is still tied to the old address.

## Resolution steps
1. Find the home move order and check its status and target date.
2. Confirm that the new address and line details on the order are correct.
3. If the order is stuck, re-submit it and request the earliest activation date.
4. Book an engineer if the new property needs a line installed.
5. Offer a mobile data add-on and a credit for the days without service.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the home move team if no activation date is available within five working days.

title: No mobile signal due to mast outage in the area
body:
# No mobile signal due to mast outage in the area

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My phone has no signal at all since yesterday.
- It says No Service on my mobile.
- I have zero bars at home where I normally have full signal.

## Likely cause
A local mast is down or under maintenance, so phones in the area show no service.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the network status map for a mast outage or planned work at the customer's postcode.
2. Confirm that the SIM is active and not barred on the account.
3. Ask the customer to try manual network selection and choose the home network.
4. Enable Wi-Fi calling so the customer can call and text over Wi-Fi during the outage.
5. Give the expected fix time and subscribe the customer to outage updates.

## When to escalate
Escalate to network operations if no outage is listed but several customers in the same area report no service.

title: Mobile data slow after reaching the fair-use limit
body:
# Mobile data slow after reaching the fair-use limit

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My mobile data has become very slow this week.
- Mobile internet is crawling even with full signal.
- Data speed on my phone dropped suddenly.

## Likely cause
The customer used the high-speed data allowance, so speed is reduced until the next billing cycle.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the data usage for the current billing cycle against the plan allowance.
2. If the fair-use limit is reached, explain that speed is reduced until the cycle resets on the bill date.
3. Offer a data add-on to restore full speed immediately.
4. Suggest a larger plan if the customer reaches the limit every month.
5. If usage is below the limit, check for a network issue at the customer's location.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the network team if usage is below the limit and speed tests stay under 1 Mbps.

title: Mobile data not working because of wrong APN settings
body:
# Mobile data not working because of wrong APN settings

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- Mobile data is not working even though I have signal.
- I can call and text but the internet does not work on my phone.
- Mobile data stopped working after I updated my phone.

## Likely cause
After a phone change or software update the APN settings are missing or wrong, so data fails even with signal.

## Resolution steps
1. Confirm that mobile data is enabled and that the plan has data allowance left.
2. Send the APN settings by text message and ask the customer to save and select them.
3. If needed, guide the customer to enter the APN manually in the mobile network settings.
4. Ask the customer to restart the phone after saving the APN.
5. Test by opening a web page with Wi-Fi switched off.

## When to escalate
Escalate to device support if data still fails with the correct APN and the SIM works in another phone.

title: Calls dropping or bad call quality because VoLTE is disabled
body:
# Calls dropping or bad call quality because VoLTE is disabled

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My calls keep dropping after a few seconds.
- Calls cut off in the middle of a conversation.
- People cannot hear me properly on calls.

## Likely cause
4G calling (VoLTE) is switched off or not provisioned, so calls fall back to a weak 2G or 3G signal and drop.

## Resolution steps
1. Check whether VoLTE is provisioned on the customer's account and enable it if it is missing.
2. Ask the customer to switch on 4G calling in the phone's mobile network settings.
3. Enable Wi-Fi calling for use indoors where signal is weak.
4. Ask the customer to update the phone software and carrier settings.
5. Check the coverage map at the customer's address for known weak areas.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the network team if calls still drop with VoLTE on and good signal.

title: New SIM not activated
body:
# New SIM not activated

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My new SIM card is not working.
- I put in the new SIM and it says SIM not provisioned.
- The new SIM has not been activated yet.

## Likely cause
The activation request for the new SIM did not complete, so the SIM is not provisioned on the network.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the SIM serial number against the order to confirm the right SIM was sent.
2. Check the activation status and re-submit the activation if it failed.
3. Ask the customer to restart the phone after about 15 minutes.
4. Make a test call and a data test with the customer on the line.
5. If the SIM is faulty, order a replacement SIM free of charge.

## When to escalate
Escalate to provisioning if activation fails twice for the same SIM.

title: Number transfer from another network delayed
body:
# Number transfer from another network delayed

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My number has not been transferred from my old network.
- The number port was supposed to happen yesterday but it has not.
- I gave my porting code a week ago and my old number is still not moved.

## Likely cause
The porting request was rejected or is on hold because the porting code or account details did not match.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the porting request status and the reason for any rejection.
2. Verify the porting code, the mobile number and the account holder name with the customer.
3. If the code has expired, ask the customer to get a new code from the old network.
4. Re-submit the port request and confirm the new port date.
5. Tell the customer to restart the phone on the port date and test calls.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the porting desk if the request is rejected twice or the delay is more than two working days.

title: Roaming not working abroad
body:
# Roaming not working abroad

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My phone is not working abroad.
- I am travelling and have no service on roaming.
- Roaming is not working, I cannot make calls or use data overseas.

## Likely cause
Roaming is not enabled on the account or the phone has not registered on a partner network.

## Resolution steps
1. Check that roaming is enabled on the account and enable it if not.
2. Check that the destination country is covered by the customer's plan.
3. Ask the customer to turn on data roaming and select a partner network manually.
4. Ask the customer to restart the phone so it registers on the partner network.
5. Offer a roaming pass and explain the charges.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the roaming team if the phone cannot register on any partner network after manual selection.

title: Unexpected roaming charges because roaming pass was not applied
body:
# Unexpected roaming charges because roaming pass was not applied

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I have been charged a huge amount for roaming.
- My bill has roaming charges even though I bought a roaming pass.
- I got a very high bill after my trip abroad.

## Likely cause
The roaming pass was not active or the customer used data outside the pass coverage, so pay-as-you-go roaming rates were charged.

## Resolution steps
1. Review the itemised bill and identify the roaming charges, dates and countries.
2. Check whether a roaming pass was active on those dates and covered that country.
3. If the pass was bought but not applied, credit the incorrect charges.
4. If the usage was outside the pass, explain the charges and offer a one-time goodwill credit as per policy.
5. Set a roaming spend cap on the account to prevent future bill shock.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the billing team for credits above the agent approval limit.

title: Charged twice in the same month
body:
# Charged twice in the same month

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I have been charged twice this month.
- Two payments were taken from my account for the same bill.
- My bill was paid twice.

## Likely cause
A manual payment and the automatic payment were both taken for the same bill.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the payment history for two payments against the same bill.
2. Confirm the dates and amounts with the customer.
3. Refund the duplicate payment to the original payment method, or leave it as credit if the customer prefers.
4. Tell the customer the refund takes three to five working days.
5. Advise the customer not to pay manually while automatic payment is active.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the payments team if the second payment does not appear in the billing system.

title: Unknown premium subscription charges on bill
body:
# Unknown premium subscription charges on bill

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- There are charges on my bill for a subscription I never signed up for.
- I am being charged every week for a premium service I do not know.
- My bill has third party charges I do not recognise.

## Likely cause
A third-party premium service was subscribed to, often by accident, and is charged to the mobile bill.

## Resolution steps
1. Find the third-party service name and short code on the itemised bill.
2. Unsubscribe the customer from the service in the billing system.
3. Apply a charge-to-bill bar so no new premium services can be added.
4. Refund charges as per the third-party charge policy.
5. Explain how to stop a service by texting STOP to the short code.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the content services team if the third party will not cancel the subscription.

title: Plan upgrade not applied until next billing cycle
body:
# Plan upgrade not applied until next billing cycle

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I upgraded my plan but I still have the old data allowance.
- My new plan is not showing in the app.
- I changed my plan yesterday and nothing has changed.

## Likely cause
The plan change was scheduled for the next bill date instead of being applied immediately.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the plan change order and its effective date.
2. If it is scheduled for the next bill date, explain this to the customer.
3. If the customer needs it now, change the order to immediate effect and explain the part-month charge.
4. Ask the customer to restart the phone and refresh the app after the change.
5. Confirm the new allowance with the customer.

## When to escalate
Escalate to billing if the order is complete but the old plan is still active after 24 hours.

title: SIM card not detected because the SIM is damaged
body:
# SIM card not detected because the SIM is damaged

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- My phone says no SIM card.
- The SIM is not being detected.
- The phone shows insert SIM even though the SIM is inside.

## Likely cause
The SIM is worn, damaged or badly seated, so the phone cannot read it.

## Resolution steps
1. Ask the customer to try the SIM in another phone to see if the SIM or the phone is at fault.
2. Check the SIM status on the account to make sure it is not blocked.
3. If the SIM fails in another phone, order a replacement SIM or issue an eSIM.
4. Activate the replacement SIM and keep the same number.
5. If the SIM works in another phone, advise the customer to have the phone's SIM slot checked.

## When to escalate
No escalation needed. Refer to the device manufacturer if the SIM slot is faulty.

title: Not receiving incoming calls because of call forwarding or do-not-disturb
body:
# Not receiving incoming calls because of call forwarding or do-not-disturb

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I am not receiving incoming calls.
- People say my phone goes straight to voicemail.
- I can make calls but nobody can call me.

## Likely cause
Call forwarding, do-not-disturb or a network call bar is sending incoming calls to voicemail.

## Resolution steps
1. Check the account for an incoming call bar and remove it if present.
2. Ask the customer to cancel all call forwarding by dialling the cancel code.
3. Check that do-not-disturb and focus modes are off and that unknown callers are not silenced.
4. Refresh the network registration by sending a provisioning update to the SIM.
5. Make a test call to the customer to confirm the phone rings.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the network team if test calls still fail after the registration refresh.

title: Verification code text messages not received
body:
# Verification code text messages not received

## Symptoms
Customers typically say things like:
- I am not receiving OTP text messages.
- Verification codes from my bank are not arriving.
- I do not get any SMS codes on my phone.

## Likely cause
Messages from short codes are blocked on the account or the phone's message centre number is wrong.

## Resolution steps
1. Check whether short-code or premium SMS is barred on the account and remove the bar.
2. Ask the customer to check the blocked senders list and the spam folder in the messages app.
3. Check and correct the message centre number on the phone.
4. Send a test short-code message to the customer.
5. Ask the customer to free up message storage if the inbox is full.

## When to escalate
Escalate to the messaging team if test short-code messages are not delivered.

title: How to power cycle a router and fibre ONT
body:
# How to power cycle a router and fibre ONT

A power cycle clears temporary faults and makes the equipment reconnect to the network.

Steps
1. Switch off the router and the fibre ONT (if there is one) at the wall.
2. Wait two full minutes.
3. Switch on the ONT first and wait until its lights are steady.
4. Switch on the router and wait up to five minutes for the internet light.

Do not ask the customer to repeat this if they have already done it in the last hour.

title: How to run a wired speed test
body:
# How to run a wired speed test

A wired test shows the real speed of the line without Wi-Fi getting in the way.

Steps
1. Connect a laptop to the router with an ethernet cable.
2. Switch off Wi-Fi on the laptop and close other apps.
3. Pause downloads and streaming on other devices.
4. Run the speed test three times at different times of day and note the results.

Compare the results with the guaranteed minimum speed on the customer's contract.

title: What the router lights mean
body:
# What the router lights mean

Power light: green means on, off means no power.
DSL or Link light: steady green means the line is in sync, flashing means it is trying to sync, off means no line signal.
Internet light: green means connected, red means the login to the network failed.
LOS light on a fibre ONT: off is normal, red means the optical signal is lost.
Wi-Fi light: on means wireless is enabled.

title: How to read your bill
body:
# How to read your bill

The bill has four parts: the monthly plan charge, one-off charges such as installation or equipment,
usage charges outside the plan such as roaming or premium services, and discounts or credits.

A first bill is often higher because it covers part of a month plus a full month in advance.
Discounts show their end date next to the discount line.

title: Priority handling for vulnerable customers
body:
# Priority handling for vulnerable customers

A customer is treated as vulnerable if they depend on the service for health or safety,
for example a medical alarm, a carer contact line, or living alone with limited mobility.

Steps
1. Add the priority flag to the account.
2. Raise any fault as a priority fault with the shortest repair target.
3. Offer a backup such as a mobile data add-on or call divert.
4. Agree a call-back time and keep the customer updated.
